subject: Sierra Labs - urgent: post-upgrade p95 spike and accuracy regressions
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sierralabs.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@sierralabs.ai>, contracts@sierralabs.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Olga —

We completed the scheduled model upgrade to the v2.1-int4 profile this morning at 06:30 PT. Within the first hour we started seeing user-facing timeouts and a 30% increase in error_rate on our ingestion pipeline. P95 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~1.2s. Separately, several users reported a rise in incorrect classifications in production scoring. This is impacting our main customer dashboard.

I need an immediate rollback or a mitigation plan. Our CS lead is on this thread and procurement has asked for an exec-level note since this may affect our renewal timeline.

I'm attaching logs and a screenshot of the p95 spike.

—Tom
Sr. Eng Manager, Production
Sierra Labs

Attachments: svc_logs_20270411.zip, p95_latency_graph.png
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sierralabs.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Tom — thank you for the flag and the artifacts. I'm sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev1.

Quick summary of immediate actions we are executing now:
- Spinning a canary route back to v2.0-int8 (the pre-upgrade baseline) for 10% of traffic to validate rollback speed.
- Triggering a temporary routing policy to prioritize low-latency pool for your workspace.
- Eng on-call (Vivek) is collecting process-level traces and NVidia metrics; we requested detailed KV cache metrics.
- Preparing a mutual action plan and exec note; will propose 30% service credit if SLA breach confirmed.

Can you confirm traffic percentage and any customer-critical routes we should push to the rollback immediately? Also, if you have a small set of failing request ids (sample) that shows misclassification, send them over — it will help isolate whether quantization introduced accuracy regression.

I'll follow up with timelines within 30 minutes.

—Olga
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Team — logs show two correlated signals: a KV cache miss storm (~4x baseline) and elevated kernel retry rates on the int4 execution path for sequences >512. The int4 codepath seems to be hitting a fallback that incurs per-token overhead. We've already started routing requests for long context sessions to v2.0-int8 to avoid the kernel regression.

I've uploaded a preliminary trace (INF-5021). Proposed short-term mitigations:
1) Full rollback to v2.0-int8 for all production routes for Sierra (estimated <8 minutes to complete).
2) If rollback violates change windows, an alternative is to disable the int4 quantization flag only for your tenant and keep v2.1 binary — this requires a hotpatch for config and is ~12-18 minutes.

I'll stand by for approval to proceed with rollback.

—Vivek
Principal SWE, Serving Runtime

Attachments referenced: p95_latency_graph.png
From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@sierralabs.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sierralabs.ai>, contracts@sierralabs.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Olga/Vivek —

We need the fastest possible path. Our ops SLA window permits emergency rollbacks. Please proceed with whatever returns latency and accuracy immediately. Also, procurement requests formal confirmation of the rollback and a proposed credit/mitigation. Our CPO has been copied in separately.

—Priya
Head of Ops, Sierra Labs
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sierralabs.ai>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@sierralabs.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, contracts@sierralabs.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Action update: we rolled Sierra Labs back to v2.0-int8 at 10:25 PT. Observed p95 returning to ~430ms within 6 minutes. Error rate back to baseline.

Next steps (near term):
- Postmortem workstream (Vivek + Karthik) to identify root cause in int4 kernel fallback path. Target initial findings 2027-04-12 16:00 PT.
- Quality validation: we will run a prioritized prompt set you provide against v2.1-int4 and v2.0-int8 and share delta metrics by EOD Monday.
- Commercial mitigation: proposing a one-time 25% invoice credit for April usage while we complete the postmortem; contracts, please confirm legal wording.
- Exec sync: 11 Apr 2027 16:00 PT — 30 minute brief. Please confirm attendees.

I've attached a short mutual action plan draft.

—Olga
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@sierralabs.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@sierralabs.ai>, contracts@sierralabs.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: scheduled model upgrade - immediate issues

Olga/Vivek — thanks for the quick rollback and the proposed remediation plan. The EOD delta report was useful — we saw a 3.2% drop in some classification buckets on v2.1-int4 vs v2.0-int8 for prompts with long context, which aligns with the kernel fallback hypothesis.

Two asks before we close this:
1) Can Redwood provide a patch ETA for the int4 fallback (we'd like a fix in the next 2 weeks if possible).
2) Can we get a formal SLA credit note for our finance team (contracts@) so we can reconcile billing?

I'll confirm exec attendees for the Thursday sync.

—Tom
Sr. Eng Manager, Production
Sierra Labs
